prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I move my preferred configuration from B035 to B011. Targeted protein degradation turns binding into elimination through a ternary complex, and the thermodynamics of that complex, especially cooperativity, give design rules that can be measured and tested. That is the physical-chemical content I look for. Many independent groups have reproduced the principle, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work are what made it rational chemistry. Crews and Deshaies supplied the founding concept and proof of principle. The principle is also distinct from earlier prizes. My own first choice, phase separation, did not gain a supporter beyond me, and the objections to it, that in-cell evidence is indirect and that credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is unresolved, are ones I made myself and cannot answer in a citation today.
statement.case_against: Maturity is the main reservation: no degrader is yet a broadly approved drug, so the clinical payoff is promised and not demonstrated, and I cannot verify trial outcomes. Credit is crowded. A trio of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli omits Sakamoto and Kim from the 2001 paper and the molecular-glue strand of Handa, Ito and Gray, so the citation must be worded narrowly to bifunctional degraders with E3 recruitment, and the omission defended openly. I still think physical chemistry and the chemistry of self-assembly are under-represented on this shortlist, and B035 would be a strong candidate once the evidence and the credit settle.

responses.point: Linke argues that a citation cannot claim more for phase separation than the evidence supports, that Pappu and Mittag are left out of any three-name split, and asks whether other first-choice members would move to B011.
responses.response: The objection is fair and I accept it. I cannot write a citation for B035 that is both honest about the debated in-cell evidence and fair to Pappu and Mittag within three names, and a prize with unresolved credit is worse than a later prize with clear names. I therefore move to B011. I agree with your wording that confines it to the degradation principle with E3 recruitment, and I would keep B035 on my alternatives list for a future round.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Handa in the trio and wants a citation covering molecular glues, since the cereblon identification is the mechanistic anchor of the glue branch.
responses.response: This is the question I put to you in round 1 and I will answer it myself. I take the cereblon work seriously, but the glue strand was explained largely in retrospect, while the PROTAC strand is a design principle with a quantitative ternary-complex basis. A citation naming both would need four or five people, and I would not give up Ciulli for Handa. I prefer the narrower citation that Aili, Aqvist and Linke propose, and I would accept a clause that acknowledges glues without crediting them.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B058 (Gray and Winkler) as a mature, physically stated mechanism, but lists B011 as an alternative and flags the narrow priority relative to Marcus, Hopfield, and Dutton and Moser.
responses.response: I understand the appeal of a mature, physically clean mechanism, and the narrowness of any B058 citation is your own concern. Dutton and Moser, Beratan and Onuchic, and Hopfield were not nominated, so a prize for Gray and Winkler would have to be drawn so carefully that it risks claiming too little. Since you already list B011 as your alternative, I ask whether you would move to it if B058 cannot reach five votes. I would be glad to have you there, given that the mechanism is reproduced and the ternary-complex cooperativity is quantitative.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks phase separation low because interpretation is debated and recognition may be premature, and holds B011 first because of the simple new principle and clinical-stage molecules.
responses.response: On timing you were right and I was wrong to argue that the debate over relevance does not signal prematurity. I still think the maturity argument cuts in both directions, since degraders also lack broad approval. The difference I now accept is that the degrader mechanism is established and reproduced, with only the clinical consequences open. For B035 the mechanism's reach in cells is what is open, which is the weaker position.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a B011 citation limited to bifunctional degraders and E3 recruitment without molecular glues, and whether Handa's supporters will accept the omission.
Whether clinical validation of degraders is sufficient by the announcement date; I cannot independently verify the latest trial outcomes.
How to treat Sakamoto and Kim, and Ito and Gray, who are omitted under any three-name trio.
Whether my own subject proximity to lipid and condensate science has made me too hard on, or too attached to, B035 and B061.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to any shortlisted candidate is apparent. My research on lipid self-assembly and amyloid is scientifically close to B035 and B061, which is subject proximity and not a recusal issue, and B011 is outside my research area. I share Lund University with Linke and Somfai and treat their views as ordinary colleague input.
